title: A local polynomial cover of an essentially finite type local algebra
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ and $(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be commutative local rings, and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a local homomorphism, meaning $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_A$. Assume that $B$ is essentially of finite type over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. There exist an integer $n\geq0$, a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset P$, and a surjective $A$-algebra map $\pi:P_{\mathfrak q}\twoheadrightarrow B$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Both $A\to P_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\pi$ are local: the inverse images of the respective maximal ideals are $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak qP_{\mathfrak q}$. Moreover, $A\to P_{\mathfrak q}$ is essentially of finite presentation, meaning that $P_{\mathfrak q}$ is a localization of a finitely presented $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra].

proof.text: By the definition of essentially finite type, choose a finite type $A$-algebra $C$, a multiplicative subset $W\subset C$, and an $A$-algebra isomorphism $W^{-1}C\cong B$. Write $j:C\to B$ for the localization map followed by this isomorphism. By the definition of finite type choose $n\geq0$ and a surjective $A$-algebra map $e:P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to C$. Put $h=j\circ e:P\to B$.

proof.text: Apply the ring localization universal property to $h$ and $P\setminus\mathfrak q$. It gives $\pi:P_{\mathfrak q}\to B$ with $\pi(f/s)=h(f)h(s)^{-1}$. This is an $A$-algebra map because its composite with $A\to P\to P_{\mathfrak q}$ is $\varphi$: this follows by evaluating the formula on constant polynomials.

source.place: Tag 0GSG (lemma-mod-injective-valuation-ring), proof, first reduction paragraph; expanded using Algebra Tags 00QM, 00F3, 00CP and 00E9

proof.text: For any $b\in B$, the fraction description gives $b=j(c)j(w)^{-1}$ with $c\in C$, $w\in W$. Lift $c,w$ to $f,s\in P$ using the surjectivity of $e$. Since $j(w)$ has inverse given by the image of $1/w$, it is a unit; the local-ring unit criterion gives $h(s)=j(w)\notin\mathfrak m_B$, hence $s\notin\mathfrak q$. Therefore $f/s\in P_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\pi(f/s)=b$. Thus $\pi$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0GSG (lemma-mod-injective-valuation-ring), proof, first reduction paragraph; expanded using Algebra Tags 00QM, 00F3, 00CP and 00E9

proof.text: The ring $P_{\mathfrak q}$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qP_{\mathfrak q}$. Each generator $f/1$ with $f\in\mathfrak q$ maps into $\mathfrak m_B$, so $\mathfrak qP_{\mathfrak q}\subseteq\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)$. The latter is proper because $\pi(1)=1$; maximality forces equality. Let $\alpha:A\to P_{\mathfrak q}$ be the structure map. Since $\pi\alpha=\varphi$, one has $\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak qP_{\mathfrak q})=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_A$. These are precisely the two required locality equalities.

source.place: Tag 0GSG (lemma-mod-injective-valuation-ring), proof, first reduction paragraph; expanded using Algebra Tags 00QM, 00F3, 00CP and 00E9

proof.text: The polynomial algebra $P$ is finitely presented over $A$: use the $n$ polynomial generators and the empty list of relations, whose ideal is zero, so the presentation is $A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(0)\cong P$. Since $P_{\mathfrak q}$ is a localization of this finitely presented algebra, $A\to P_{\mathfrak q}$ is essentially of finite presentation in the stated sense (Stacks Tag 00QM). This also covers $n=0$.
